stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Oct 2023 cross-border fire
frames.note: The story begins when Hezbollah opened a cross-border front in solidarity with Gaza after Oct 7, 2023, drawing Israeli return fire. Under this frame, the current strikes and disarmament pressure read as the unfinished resolution of a war Hezbollah chose to enter. US, Israeli, and most Western diplomatic readouts open with this start date.

frames.label: 2006 war and UNSCR 1701
frames.note: The story begins with the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war and the UN Security Council Resolution 1701 framework that was supposed to disarm Hezbollah south of the Litani. Under this frame, today's standoff reads as a 20-year failure of an unenforced ceasefire architecture. UN officials, EU diplomats, and Lebanese state institutions tend to open here.

frames.label: 1982 Israeli invasion
frames.note: The story begins with Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon and the occupation that birthed Hezbollah as a resistance movement. Under this frame, current strikes and the demand to disarm read as the latest chapter of a four-decade occupation cycle. Hezbollah, Iranian state media, and much of the Lebanese Shia public open with this start date.

bands.label: Ceasefire that does not hold
bands.summary: Successive US-brokered truces are announced while Israeli strikes, ground operations, and an Israeli ministerial pledge to stay for years continue across southern Lebanon.

nodes.title: US-brokered ceasefire announced after deadly flare-up
nodes.what: After four Israeli soldiers were killed in southern Lebanon and Israel responded with fresh airstrikes, US mediators announced that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to a renewed ceasefire. Israeli officials said they were committed to the truce as long as Hezbollah did not attack, while Hezbollah's leader said Israel would eventually be expelled from 'every inch' of Lebanese territory.

nodes.title: Lebanese Health Ministry reports near-4,000 dead since escalation
nodes.what: The Lebanese Health Ministry reported that the cumulative death toll from Israeli attacks since the start of the escalation had reached 3,980, with 23 killed in a single day of strikes in southern Lebanon. The figures were issued as ceasefire announcements circulated in Beirut and Washington.

nodes.title: Strikes continue across south Lebanon despite reported truce
nodes.what: Israeli strikes hit Nabatieh and other parts of southern Lebanon, killing at least 16 people, including the well-known turtle conservationist Mona Khalil. Medecins Sans Frontieres described conditions in Nabatieh as resembling a 'death trap,' and the cumulative toll reported by Lebanese authorities crossed 4,000.
nodes.disputed: Israeli officials described the strikes as responses to specific Hezbollah activity and said the ceasefire held conditionally; Al Jazeera, Lebanese authorities and the Guardian described the same strikes as continued Israeli attacks during what was meant to be a truce.

nodes.title: Israel orders army to cease fire but remain in position
nodes.what: Israel's government ordered its army to cease fire in Lebanon while keeping troops in their current positions, according to Israeli television. The Israeli ambassador to the US said Israel was committed to a new ceasefire but that its forces would stay on Lebanese soil, and BBC reporters were shown destroyed villages inside the Israeli-held southern strip.

nodes.title: UK condemns Israeli minister over Lebanon remarks
nodes.what: The UK foreign secretary publicly condemned Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's comments about Lebanon as 'horrendous and abhorrent.' The exchange marked a visible widening of diplomatic strain between Israel and a Western government over ministerial statements on Lebanon.

nodes.title: Israeli minister Smotrich says forces will stay in Lebanon for years
nodes.what: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich publicly said Israeli forces would remain in Lebanon for years, openly contradicting US efforts to negotiate an Israeli withdrawal under the ceasefire framework. On the same day, Israeli forces struck southern Lebanon again, an Israeli soldier was killed and 13 wounded in an overnight operation, and Lebanese sources reported dozens of further deaths.
nodes.disputed: Press TV and other outlets aligned with Hezbollah framed Smotrich's statement as confirmation of an open-ended occupation; the Taipei Times and Israeli readouts framed continued operations as enforcement of ceasefire terms against Hezbollah infiltration.

bands.label: Open war and first ceasefire
bands.summary: Israel escalates to full air and ground war against Hezbollah, kills its senior leadership, and signs a first US-mediated ceasefire in late 2024 that frays through 2025 and 2026.

nodes.title: Pager and handheld radio explosions across Lebanon
nodes.what: Over two days, thousands of pagers and walkie-talkies used by Hezbollah members detonated almost simultaneously in Beirut, the Bekaa, and southern Lebanon, killing dozens including civilians and wounding thousands. Lebanese officials and Western reporting attributed the operation to Israel; Israel did not formally claim it at the time.

nodes.title: Israel kills Hezbollah secretary-general Hassan Nasrallah
nodes.what: An Israeli airstrike on Hezbollah's underground headquarters beneath Beirut's southern suburbs killed Hassan Nasrallah, who had led the movement since 1992. Heavy bunker-penetrating bombs were used and several other senior commanders died alongside him.

nodes.title: Israeli ground forces cross into southern Lebanon
nodes.what: Israel announced what it described as a limited, localized ground operation into southern Lebanon, with troops entering across multiple sectors of the border. Air and artillery strikes simultaneously expanded across Beirut, the Bekaa Valley, and the south, displacing more than a million people inside Lebanon.

nodes.title: Naim Qassem named Hezbollah secretary-general
nodes.what: Hezbollah's Shura Council selected longtime deputy Naim Qassem as its new secretary-general after the killings of Nasrallah and his presumed successor Hashem Safieddine. Qassem said the movement would continue confronting Israel and would assess any ceasefire on its own terms.

nodes.title: US-mediated ceasefire takes effect
nodes.what: A 60-day ceasefire brokered by the United States with French support came into force. Hezbollah forces and weapons were to move north of the Litani River, the Lebanese Armed Forces were to deploy into the south, and Israeli troops were to withdraw within the same window, with UN Security Council Resolution 1701 cited as the framework.
nodes.disputed: US and Israeli statements describe the agreement as a binding step toward disarming Hezbollah south of the Litani; Hezbollah and allied Lebanese officials describe it as a halt to hostilities tied to full Israeli withdrawal, not a standalone disarmament commitment.

nodes.title: Ceasefire frays through 2025 and into 2026
nodes.what: Israeli airstrikes and targeted operations continued across southern Lebanon and the Bekaa through 2025 and the first half of 2026, with Israeli forces remaining at several positions inside Lebanese territory past the original withdrawal date. Lebanese authorities, UNIFIL, and rights monitors reported repeated civilian casualties.
nodes.disputed: Israeli officials present continued strikes as enforcement against Hezbollah ceasefire breaches and reconstitution; the Lebanese government and UN bodies present the same strikes and the ongoing Israeli presence as violations of the ceasefire and of Lebanese sovereignty.

bands.label: Solidarity front with Gaza
bands.summary: After Oct 7, Hezbollah opens daily cross-border fire from south Lebanon and Israel responds, displacing tens of thousands on both sides of the Blue Line.

nodes.title: Hezbollah opens cross-border front day after Oct 7
nodes.what: One day after the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, Hezbollah fired guided anti-tank missiles and artillery at Israeli positions in the disputed Shebaa Farms area, declaring solidarity with Gaza. Israel returned fire with artillery and air strikes, and a pattern of daily exchanges across the Blue Line began. Hezbollah cast the fire as a limited support front; Israel treated it as an open second front.

nodes.title: Mass displacement on both sides of the Blue Line
nodes.what: As exchanges intensified through October and November, Israel ordered the evacuation of communities along its northern border including Kiryat Shmona, and tens of thousands of residents of south Lebanese villages fled north. UN agencies reported sustained displacement on the Lebanese side, with schools and clinics in border areas shutting down for the remainder of the period.

nodes.title: Strike in Beirut suburb kills Hamas deputy Saleh al-Arouri
nodes.what: A drone strike in Dahieh, a southern Beirut suburb considered a Hezbollah stronghold, killed Hamas deputy political chief Saleh al-Arouri and six others. Israel did not formally claim the strike at the time. The hit deep inside Beirut, far from the border exchange zone, was treated by Lebanese officials as a major widening of the front.
nodes.disputed: Israeli officials briefed anonymously that the strike targeted Hamas leadership operating outside Gaza; Hezbollah and the Lebanese government described it as an Israeli attack on Lebanese sovereignty and a deliberate escalation.

nodes.title: Deeper strikes, wildfires, and US shuttle diplomacy
nodes.what: Israeli strikes reached further into south Lebanon and Hezbollah projectiles set off wildfires across northern Israel, deepening the displacement crisis on both sides. US envoy Amos Hochstein shuttled between Beirut and Jerusalem to prevent a slide into open war while Gaza ceasefire talks stalled, and Israeli officials publicly warned that a northern campaign was being prepared.

nodes.title: Strike in Beirut kills Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr
nodes.what: An Israeli air strike on the Dahieh suburb of Beirut killed Fuad Shukr, a senior Hezbollah military commander. Israel said Shukr was responsible for a rocket strike days earlier that killed twelve children and teenagers in the Druze town of Majdal Shams in the Israeli-held Golan. It was the first openly claimed Israeli strike on the Beirut suburbs since the 2006 war.

nodes.title: Pager and walkie-talkie attacks across Lebanon
nodes.what: On Sep 17 and 18, thousands of pagers and then handheld radios used by Hezbollah members detonated nearly simultaneously across Lebanon, killing dozens and wounding several thousand, including civilians and children. Lebanese authorities and Hezbollah attributed the operation to Israel; Israeli officials did not formally claim it at the time. The attacks immediately preceded a broader Israeli air campaign.
nodes.disputed: Israeli commentary described the operation as a precision strike against an armed organization's command network; Lebanese authorities and UN human rights officials described it as an indiscriminate attack on a civilian environment that wounded and maimed bystanders.

bands.label: 1701 era and frozen front
bands.summary: The 2006 war ends with UN Security Council Resolution 1701 and a UNIFIL-monitored buffer that is widely seen as unenforced, while Hezbollah grows into Lebanon's dominant armed and political force.

nodes.title: Hezbollah cross-border raid triggers 2006 war
nodes.what: Hezbollah fighters crossed the Blue Line, killed several Israeli soldiers and captured two, prompting Israel to launch a 34-day air and ground campaign against Hezbollah positions and Lebanese infrastructure. The war killed more than 1,100 people in Lebanon and around 165 in Israel, and displaced roughly a million Lebanese and several hundred thousand Israelis. It set the template for every later cross-border escalation.

nodes.title: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 1701
nodes.what: The Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 1701, calling for a full cessation of hostilities, an expanded UNIFIL deployment, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon, and the disarmament of all armed groups so that only the Lebanese state would hold weapons south of the Litani River. The ceasefire took effect on 14 August 2006 and became the legal frame every later round of fighting is measured against.

nodes.title: Doha Agreement ends the political crisis
nodes.what: Lebanese factions meeting in Qatar agreed to elect army chief Michel Suleiman as president, form a national unity government in which the Hezbollah-led opposition received veto power, and adopt a new electoral law. The deal ended an 18-month presidential vacancy and stabilized institutions, but it also entrenched Hezbollah's status as an armed party inside the state rather than resolving the question of its weapons.

nodes.title: Israel launches Operation Northern Shield against cross-border tunnels
nodes.what: The Israeli army began an open operation to locate and destroy attack tunnels it said Hezbollah had dug from southern Lebanon into northern Israel, eventually announcing the discovery of six tunnels. UNIFIL later confirmed that at least some of the tunnels crossed the Blue Line in violation of Resolution 1701, sharpening international focus on Hezbollah's military buildup along the border.

bands.label: Invasion, occupation, resistance
bands.summary: Israel invades Lebanon in 1982, occupies the south for 18 years, Hezbollah forms as an armed resistance, and Israel withdraws in 2000 leaving disputed border points.

nodes.title: Israel invades Lebanon
nodes.what: Israeli forces launched Operation Peace for Galilee, crossing into Lebanon to expel the Palestine Liberation Organization. Within weeks Israeli troops reached Beirut and began a siege of the western part of the city, which ended with the PLO's evacuation in August.

nodes.title: UN Security Council Resolution 1559
nodes.what: The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 1559, calling for the withdrawal of all foreign forces from Lebanon and the disarmament of all Lebanese and non-Lebanese militias. The resolution targeted Syrian troops then in Lebanon and is also cited as the basis for later demands that Hezbollah disarm.
